b: Features : Failure to thrive (FTT), polyuria, nephrocalcinosis, short stature, mental retardation.
Electrolyte Imbalance : Hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis, renal salt wasting, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, hypercalciuria.
Cause : Sporadic or autosomal recessive (AR) mutation.
Pathophysiology :Overactivation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and hyperplasia of the juxtaglomerular apparatus .
Increased production of prostaglandin E2 in the kidney.
Mechanism : Defective mTAL transport (NKCCT, ROMK1, CLCKB)

qs.q: What is the primary renal mechanism and expected electrolyte abnormality in a patient suffering from Bartter's syndrome?
o: Enhanced ENaC sodium reabsorption causing hypertension
Defective thick ascending limb transport causing hypokalemia
Impaired distal tubule transport causing hypocalciuria
qs.e: Bartter's syndrome involves a defective medullary thick ascending limb transport mechanism similar to the effect of furosemide, leading to failure to concentrate urine, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis. Gitelman's syndrome instead involves the distal convoluted tubule and causes hypocalciuria.
